content:
Maya - Support: Evan from Acme reports 401s after migrating their app to a Dedicated instance inside a VPC. They say token is valid; traces show LB -> istio-ingressgateway -> extauth-proxy -> redwood-gateway. Authorization header present at LB but missing by the time it hits redwood-gateway. Anyone seen istio/ingress rewrite auth headers like this?

Evan (Acme): Confirmed. Captured headers at LB: 
```
Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi
Host: acme-dedicated.redwood.example
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.12
```
But gateway logs show request with no Authorization header and we get 401. No rotation or token scope issues on our side.

deploy-bot: deploy redwood-gateway/2024-06-15T12:18:32 succeeded in us-west-2 :rocket:

Tom - Eng Infra: This smells like ext_authz or the ingressgateway filter chain dropping/normalizing headers after auth. Quick ask: can you paste the istio-ingressgateway Envoy config dump around http_filters? Also, try a simple curl that hits the ingress and show -v output.

Evan (Acme): Repro curl:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi" https://acme-dedicated.redwood.example/v1/chat
```
Response: 401, server says missing credentials.

Maya - Support: I ran a quick reproduction from our test pod into their VPC (same gw) and saw the same: LB receives auth header, istio-ingressgateway access log shows auth header present, but upstream to redwood-gateway the header is absent.

Sara - Platform: Two probable areas: (1) Istio ext_authz returning and Envoy configured to strip the header on success, or (2) an internal sidecar or auth proxy (authz-proxy) intentionally rewrites Authorization into a cookie or x-forwarded-authorization. Check istio AuthorizationPolicy / RequestAuthentication + ext_authz config for any "remove_headers" or header manipulation rules.

Tom - Eng Infra: Agreed. On Envoy, extauth filter has options to remove headers after check. If you can get the filter config dump, look for: 
```
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
    failure_mode_allow: false
    include_request_headers_in_check: true
    allowed_upstream_headers_on_success: []   # empty == strips everything
```
If allowed_upstream_headers_on_success is empty, Envoy strips all request headers that ext_authz doesn't explicitly allow. That would drop Authorization.

Evan (Acme): We don't currently have access to the gateway config but can ask infra. Is there a quick mitigation?

Maya - Support: Short-term workaround: have the ingress/edge add a duplicate header before extauth runs, e.g. X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer ... and configure redwood-gateway to accept x-forwarded-authorization if present. Long-term: allow Authorization in allowed_upstream_headers_on_success.

Tom - Eng Infra: Yep. Kubernetes patch we used previously: add this to the ext_authz filter config (pseudo yaml):
```
allowed_upstream_headers_on_success:
  - authorization
  - x-request-id
```
Or set it to preserve specific headers. We'll need a controlled rollout.

Sara - Platform: I'll open a short-lived canary to add authorization to the allowed list on staging ingress to validate. If that fixes it, we'll coordinate a safe PROD change and a note for customers about the behavior.

Maya - Support: I've filed SUP-8742 and attached Evan's trace + curl output. Assigned to Eng Infra (Tom) to triage ext_authz config and Platform (Sara) to coordinate canary. Evan, we'll keep you in the loop.

Evan (Acme): Thanks all — would appreciate ETA, this is blocking their by-weekly sync.

Tom - Eng Infra: Will try to get a staging patch by EOD Pacific. If we can't change filter safely, we'll propose the header-duplication workaround for you to configure on your LB (add X-Forwarded-Authorization).

Maya - Support: Adding notes for runbook: check envoy config dump for ext_authz.allowed_upstream_headers_on_success, look for any custom auth proxy that rewrites headers, and as stopgap use x-forwarded-authorization mapping.

Sara - Platform: Also note: if customers use mTLS between ingress and gateways, some proxies strip sensitive headers when mutual auth is in use; verify LB -> ingress connection mode too.

Maya - Support: Closing loop for now — updates will appear in SUP-8742. :white_check_mark:
